elements.element: If the automatic-renewal alternative is not used, renewal may occur only by mutual written agreement of both parties.
elements.evidence: Article IV(I) states that the Agreement “may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties.” Articles IV(II) and (III) also condition extensions on mutual written agreement.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal alternative is used, each automatic renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: Met as a conditional requirement because automatic renewal is demonstrably absent: renewal is permitted only by a new mutual written agreement.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal alternative is used, Customer may opt out on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Met as a conditional requirement because the clause excludes automatic renewal and therefore does not invoke the automatic-renewal opt-out requirement.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal alternative is used, Vendor must provide a reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Met as a conditional requirement because the clause excludes automatic renewal and therefore does not invoke the reminder requirement.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal alternative is used, renewal price increases must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Met as a conditional requirement because the clause selects the mutual-written-agreement branch rather than the automatic-renewal branch.
The clause requires mutual written agreement for renewal and contains no automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.element: The automatic-renewal non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: No automatic-renewal mechanism or non-renewal notice window is stated.

elements.element: Renewal price increases are capped at 5% or less.
elements.evidence: The operative clause contains no renewal price-increase cap.

result.reason: The operative text selects the first preferred alternative by replacing Licensor's unilateral seven-year option with renewal only by mutual written agreement. Accordingly, the automatic-renewal safeguards are conditionally inapplicable. The fallback independently fails because there is no automatic renewal, notice window, or 5% price cap. The change is narrow and leaves unrelated termination and payment provisions intact. Drafting quality is materially impaired because Article IV(II) remains grammatically incomplete (“mutual written of the parties”) and the renewal provisions are unnecessarily repetitive, although Articles IV(I) and (III) make the mutual-agreement requirement clear.
